=== orchestrator
Culprit's run loop: baselines → discriminating tasks → noise-aware bisect → intent (PRD §7, §8).

The loop is deterministic and memoised in the ledger, so running it again for an existing
run_id resumes it: completed steps and task runs are reused, never re-executed.
=== bisect
Deterministic bisect controller with `git bisect skip` semantics (PRD §8.1).

The controller knows nothing about evals: it asks `classify(sha)` for GOOD, BAD or SKIP and
narrows the range. `good` is implicitly GOOD and the last candidate (`bad`) is implicitly BAD.
=== stats
Wilson score interval and the deterministic GOOD / BAD / INCONCLUSIVE rule (PRD §8.2).
=== baseline
Measure both ends of the range (v2: staged and reused).

v1 ran every task × k on the good and the bad commit: 26 tasks × 3 × 2 = 156 victim runs, the most
expensive part of a run. v2 does it in two stages:

1. **Screen**: every task × 1 (repetition 0) on both ends (step kind `baseline`).
2. **Full k**: repetitions 1..k-1, on both ends, only for tasks that did not pass on both ends in
   the screen (step kind `baseline:full`). Those are the tasks that differ, and the ones that may be
   flaky or broken on both sides. A task that passed once on each end gets no more runs.

Both ends always run the same (task, repetition) set, so the regression gate compares like with
like, and it uses exactly the runs that were made: n is the real count, not tasks × k. The
selection rule is symmetric in good and bad (swap the labels and the same tasks are chosen), so
under "no regression" it can't favour one side. It can miss a task that drops from good to bad but
happened to pass once on the bad end; the other dropped tasks still carry the signal.

Before each stage, results already measured for the same commit in an earlier matching run are
copied in (culprit.reuse), so only the gaps run.
=== localise
Localiser: which hunk of the culprit commit is responsible (PRD §8.3).

1. Split the culprit diff into hunks.
2. An LLM ranks them from the diff, the commit's (leak-filtered) intent and the failing tasks.
3. The top-N hunks are reverse-applied one at a time on the culprit commit and re-tested on the
   discriminating tasks; the first revert that flips BAD → GOOD is the responsible hunk. If none
   does, pairs are tried (capped), then the answer falls back to the whole commit.

`culprit localise <run_id>` runs this on a finished run whose culprit was found. Baselines and
bisect steps come from the ledger; each revert is judged like a bisect step (Wilson rule,
resampling, budget, resume) under its own step kinds, `localise:h<N>`.
=== fix
Fixer and Verifier (PRD §8.4, §10): `culprit fix <run_id>` on a localised run.

The Fixer (one structured LLM call per attempt) sees the responsible hunks, the commit's leak-filtered
intent, the telling tasks' results and the affected files at the bad head. It names the gain the
commit was after (latency, tokens, cost or none) and returns exact search-and-replace edits that
restore the lost behaviour without reverting the commit. Edits may touch only the responsible
hunks' files, never the suite.

The Verifier applies the patch at the bad head and runs the full suite plus the held-out tasks × k.
A fix is verified only if all three gates hold (PRD §10):
1. quality: its Wilson interval reaches the good baseline's (upper bound ≥ good's lower bound);
2. intended gain kept: the named metric is no worse than at bad by more than the tolerance;
3. no new failures: no task that passes every repetition at good fails every repetition with the fix.
A failed attempt is fed back to the next one. After the last attempt fails, the responsible hunks'
revert is verified at the bad head the same way, as the fallback.
=== drift
Drift check: `culprit drift --ref <known-good ref>`. "Did we break it, or did the world change?"

A victim run is determined by the commit, the suite, the victim model, the eval runner and the seed.
When a commit that once passed now fails with all of those unchanged, the cause is outside the repo:
the model behind the API, a provider or tool service. So the check re-runs the ref fresh, with the
same suite snapshot, model, k and seeds as a recorded baseline of it, and compares the two with
one-sided Fisher tests in both directions:

- `drifted`: the ref passes less now than it did (p_worse < alpha). Bisecting your history won't help;
  the same code got worse.
- `improved`: it passes more now (p_better < alpha).
- `stable`: neither.

Per-task changes say where. Nothing from the recorded baseline is reused: the point is to measure again.
=== ci
CI regression gate: `culprit ci --base <ref> --head <ref>`, and the PR comment it posts.

On a pull request: measure the PR's head against its base (the regression gate). Clean → exit 0.
Regressed → bisect the PR's commits to the culprit, optionally localise the responsible hunk and
propose a verified fix, write a markdown comment for the PR, and exit 1 so the check fails. Anything
that stops the run (budget, infrastructure, error) → exit 2, so a flaky API never blames a commit.

`comment(ledger, run_id)` builds the comment from the ledger alone, so `culprit comment <run_id>`
renders it for any finished run at no cost. See `examples/github-action/culprit.yml`.
=== audit
Eval blind-spot audit: `culprit audit --ref <ref>`. "Which realistic regressions would our evals miss?"

Mutation testing for agents. Culprit makes realistic, plausible-looking changes to the agent at `ref`
(mutants), each in its own throwaway worktree, never committed anywhere, and runs the eval suite on
each. A mutant is **caught** when the suite passes significantly less than at the unchanged ref
(one-sided Fisher p < alpha) and **missed** otherwise. The mutation score is caught / valid mutants;
every missed mutant comes with an idea for an eval task that would catch it.

Mutants come from:
- `--operators`: a catalogue of regression patterns (below). For each, one structured model call
  reads the agent's source and returns exact search-and-replace edits (the Fixer's safe edit format),
  plus a one-line summary and a task idea, or says the pattern doesn't apply.
- `--patches DIR`: your own `*.patch` files (deterministic, no model).

Proposals are stored in the run before anything is evaluated, so a rerun with `--run-id` resumes
without asking the model again. A mutant that doesn't apply or no longer installs is reported
`invalid` and left out of the score.
=== entire
Commit intent from Entire (`entire checkpoint explain <sha>`), with leakage filter and fallback.

Only the context of the commit under examination is fetched, never its neighbours. Before any
Entire text reaches an LLM, lines that could leak benchmark labels are stripped and counted.
=== suite
Pinned eval suite: every commit in a run is judged by the same tasks.

The suite comes from one snapshot, either a directory at a victim ref (default `evals/` at `main`)
or a directory on disk. It is materialised once under `.culprit/suites/` and copied into each
worktree before evaluation, replacing whatever suite that commit had. The ledger records the
snapshot (commit SHA, or content digest for a path), and resume reuses that snapshot even if
the ref has moved since.
=== report
`culprit report <run_id>`: a run's receipts as markdown and a static HTML page (PRD M6).

Everything comes from the ledger: verdict, baselines and the regression gate, the bisect timeline
with each commit's Wilson interval against its threshold, skipped commits, the culprit's intent and
diff, neatlogs trace IDs, costs, and where reused baseline results came from. The victim repo is
only read for commit subjects and positions; without it the report still renders.

"""Wilson score interval and the deterministic GOOD / BAD / INCONCLUSIVE rule (PRD §8.2)."""
from __future__ import annotations
import math
from enum import StrEnum
class Decision(StrEnum):
    GOOD = "GOOD"
    BAD = "BAD"
    INCONCLUSIVE = "INCONCLUSIVE"
def wilson(passes: int, n: int, z: float = 1.96) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """95% (by default) Wilson score interval for `passes` successes in `n` trials."""
    if n <= 0:
        return 0.0, 1.0
    if not 0 <= passes <= n:
        raise ValueError(f"passes={passes} outside [0, {n}]")
    p = passes / n
    z2 = z * z
    denom = 1 + z2 / n
    centre = (p + z2 / (2 * n)) / denom
    half = z * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z2 / (4 * n * n)) / denom
    return max(0.0, centre - half), min(1.0, centre + half)
def decide(passes: int, n: int, threshold: float, z: float = 1.96) -> tuple[Decision, float, float]:
    low, high = wilson(passes, n, z)
    if low >= threshold:
        return Decision.GOOD, low, high
    if high <= threshold:
        return Decision.BAD, low, high
    return Decision.INCONCLUSIVE, low, high
def intervals_overlap(a: tuple[float, float], b: tuple[float, float]) -> bool:
    return a[0] <= b[1] and b[0] <= a[1]
def fisher_one_sided(good_passes: int, good_n: int, bad_passes: int, bad_n: int) -> float:
    """One-sided Fisher exact p-value for "good passes more often than bad".
    Checking whether two 95% intervals overlap is far stricter than a 5% test: 57/60 vs 48/60
    overlaps, so a regression breaking 3 of 20 tasks would be called noise. This is the exact
    test on the same 2×2 table: P(good would score at least `good_passes` if both had one rate).
    """
    total_pass, n = good_passes + bad_passes, good_n + bad_n
    denom = math.comb(n, total_pass)
    upper = min(good_n, total_pass)
    return sum(math.comb(good_n, x) * math.comb(bad_n, total_pass - x)
               for x in range(good_passes, upper + 1)) / denom

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Baselines:
    good: StepResult
    bad: StepResult

    def threshold(self, runs: list[TaskRun]) -> float:
        """Midpoint of the good and bad pass rates over the same task mix as `runs` (PRD §8.1 step 2)."""
        g, b = self.good.task_rates(), self.bad.task_rates()

---
title: Introduction
description: Culprit finds the commit that made your AI agent worse, using your own eval suite and real statistics, then explains it and verifies a fix.
---

## What Culprit does

Your agent passed its evals last week. Today it fails some of them, and there are dozens of commits in
between: prompt edits, refactors, dependency bumps, "make it faster" changes. Culprit is
`git bisect` for that situation. You give it a good ref and a bad ref, and it:

1. **Checks the drop is real.** It runs your suite at both ends, several times, and stops if a
   one-sided Fisher test can't tell good from bad. Noise never gets a commit blamed.
2. **Bisects with statistics.** Each step runs the tasks that dropped several times and decides GOOD
   or BAD from a 95% confidence interval, resampling when the answer is unclear. A commit that won't
   install is skipped, as `git bisect skip` does.
3. **Explains the culprit.** It reads why the change was made, from the coding-agent session behind the
   commit when one was recorded, or from the commit message and diff.
4. **Finds the lines.** It reverts the commit's hunks one at a time, then in pairs, until the agent
   recovers.
5. **Writes a fix and proves it.** It proposes the smallest change that restores the behaviour while
   keeping what the commit was for, and verifies it on your full suite plus held-out tasks.

Everything runs on your machine with your own model key. Every agent run and decision is stored in a
local ledger, so a verdict can be audited and a stopped run resumed.

## When to use it

- **An eval score dropped** and you don't know which change caused it.
- **On every pull request**, as a check that fails only on a real regression and comments with the
  culprit. See [CI and pull requests](/docs/ci/).
- **When nothing in your code changed** but results did. `culprit drift` tells you whether the model
  behind the API moved. See [Drift checks](/docs/drift/).
- **Before you trust your evals.** `culprit audit` makes realistic regressions and shows which ones your
  suite would miss. See [Auditing your evals](/docs/audit/).

## How it fits your project

Culprit doesn't need an SDK or changes to your agent's code. It needs three things your repo
probably has already, or can add in a few minutes:

- a git history with a good ref and a bad ref,
- a uv project with a committed `uv.lock`, so any commit can be installed,
- an eval suite, and a module that runs one task and prints one JSON line.

[Prepare your agent](/docs/prepare-your-agent/) covers the details.

## Results so far

Culprit was measured on three agents with planted regressions and known answers: 54 scored bisects
across 5 victim models, **51 correct, 3 missed and none naming a wrong commit**. The misses were on
a small model too noisy for the gate to confirm the drop. [Limits](/docs/limits/) lists what these
results don't show.

## Next steps

[[cards]]

- [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart/): install, set up and run your first bisect in five minutes.
- [Prepare your agent](/docs/prepare-your-agent/): the eval module and suite Culprit expects.
- [How bisect works](/docs/how-bisect-works/): the gate, the intervals and the decision rule.
- [CLI reference](/docs/cli/): every command and option.

---
title: Quickstart
description: Install Culprit, set up your agent's repo and find your first culprit commit.
---

You need Python 3.12 or newer, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git, and an API key from
[Anthropic](https://console.anthropic.com/) or [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/).

[[steps]]

1. **Install Culprit.**

    ```bash
    uv tool install culprit-cli
    ```

    This puts the `culprit` command on your `PATH`. Just trying it? `uvx culprit-cli init` runs it
    without installing.

2. **Set up your agent's repo.** Run this anywhere inside it:

    ```bash
    culprit init
    ```

    The first time, it asks which provider your key is for, the key itself, and an optional
    neatlogs key for tracing. They're saved once for all your repos. Then it finds your eval module,
    counts your tasks, writes `culprit.toml` and offers to run one task to check its output.

    ```console
    Setting up /home/you/refund-agent
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: from culprit init
      your agent will run on z-ai/glm-5.3 via openrouter during a bisect
      eval modules found: refund_agent.eval
      26 tasks in evals/: refund_small_order, refund_timeout_once, …
      added .culprit/ to .gitignore
      wrote /home/you/refund-agent/culprit.toml
      check passed: task refund_small_order: passed=True (cost=0.0021, latency_ms=7086)
    ```

    If `init` can't find an eval module, see [Prepare your agent](/docs/prepare-your-agent/).

3. **Find the commit.** Give it a ref that was good and one that is bad:

    ```bash
    culprit run --good v1.0 --bad HEAD --budget-usd 3
    ```

    Culprit measures both ends, checks the drop is real, then bisects:

    ```console
    run 77f60c9fccf8: 14 commits in v1.0..HEAD, 10 tasks × 3
      screen ×1: good 9/10, bad 5/10; full k=3 on 5 tasks
      good 19/20 CI [0.76, 0.99]  bad 6/20 CI [0.15, 0.52]
      regression gate: one-sided Fisher p=0.0000 (alpha 0.05)
      discriminating tasks: t02, t04, t05, t01, t03
      4ebe03f827 install failed → SKIP
      464e05fa11 'revert requests pin': 14/15 CI [0.70, 0.99] vs t=0.50 → GOOD
      462db36ee1 'docs: maintenance note 11': 1/15 CI [0.01, 0.30] vs t=0.50 → BAD
      a6b1a67aaf 'docs: maintenance note 9': 14/15 CI [0.70, 0.99] vs t=0.50 → GOOD
      e38a2b4ed8 'speed up tool handling': 1/15 CI [0.01, 0.30] vs t=0.50 → BAD
    Culprit: e38a2b4ed865a45a70d0ac149aa88204610620a8 'speed up tool handling' (confidence: 95% Wilson)
    ```

    The run ID on the first line is what the next commands take.

4. **Find the lines and fix them.**

    ```bash
    culprit localise 77f60c9fccf8   # which hunks of the commit are responsible
    culprit fix 77f60c9fccf8        # a minimal fix, verified on the full suite and held-out tasks
    ```

5. **Read the report.**

    ```bash
    culprit report 77f60c9fccf8
    ```

    This writes `.culprit/reports/report-77f60c9fccf8.md` and `.html`: the verdict, the regression
    gate, every bisect step with its interval, the commit's intent and diff, and the cost.

!!! tip "No regression is a real answer"
    If the gate can't show the bad ref is worse, `culprit run` ends with `no_regression` and blames
    nothing. That's the right outcome when the drop was noise, or when your model doesn't trip over
    the change. See [How bisect works](/docs/how-bisect-works/#outcomes).

## What it costs

You pay your provider for your agent's runs and for Culprit's own model calls. On our 26-task test
agent with 3 runs per task, a bisect cost between $0.04 and $0.41 depending on the model.
`--budget-usd` is a hard cap; a stopped run continues with `culprit resume`. See
[Cost and budgets](/docs/cost-and-budgets/).

## Next steps

[[cards]]

- [CI and pull requests](/docs/ci/): run the regression gate on every PR.
- [Configuration](/docs/configuration/): keys, models and `culprit.toml`.

---
title: Installation
description: Install the culprit command with uv, pipx or pip, and keep it up to date.
---

## Requirements

- **Python 3.12 or newer.**
- **[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).** Culprit installs your agent at each commit with
  `uv sync --locked`, so uv must be on your `PATH` even if you install Culprit another way.
- **git.**
- **An API key** from Anthropic or OpenRouter. See [Configuration](/docs/configuration/#keys).

Culprit runs on macOS and Linux. Windows hasn't been tested.

## Install

The package is `culprit-cli` on PyPI; the command it installs is `culprit`.

=== "uv (recommended)"

```bash
uv tool install culprit-cli
```

uv installs it in its own environment and puts `culprit` on your `PATH`. If the command isn't
found afterwards, run `uv tool update-shell` and open a new terminal.

Other ways work too:

```bash
pipx install culprit-cli     # also an isolated environment
pip install culprit-cli      # into the current environment
```

### Try it without installing

```bash
uvx culprit-cli init
uvx culprit-cli run --good v1.0 --bad HEAD
```

`uvx` downloads Culprit into a temporary environment and runs it. Each command needs the
`culprit-cli` prefix, so install it if you'll use it more than once.

## Check it works

```bash
culprit --help
```

You should see the list of commands, starting with `run`.

## Upgrade

```bash
uv tool upgrade culprit-cli
```

With pipx, `pipx upgrade culprit-cli`; with pip, `pip install -U culprit-cli`. The
[changelog](/docs/changelog/) lists what changed.

## Uninstall

```bash
uv tool uninstall culprit-cli
```

Culprit also leaves two kinds of files behind, which you can delete:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Saved keys | `~/.config/culprit/credentials.env` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/culprit/`) |
| Run state: ledger, worktrees, reports | `.culprit/` in each repo you ran it in |
| Settings | `culprit.toml` in each repo you set up |

## Next steps

[[cards]]

- [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart/): your first bisect.
- [Prepare your agent](/docs/prepare-your-agent/): what your repo needs.

---
title: Prepare your agent
nav: Prepare your agent
description: The three things Culprit needs from your agent's repo: an installable history, an eval suite, and a module that runs one task.
---

Culprit doesn't import your agent or need an SDK. At each commit it checks out a worktree, installs
it, and runs your eval module once per task and repetition. Your repo needs three things.

## 1. An installable history

- **A git repository** with a ref that was good (a tag, branch or commit) and one that is bad.
- **A uv project with a committed `uv.lock`.** Culprit installs each commit with `uv sync --locked`
  in its own worktree under `.culprit/worktrees/`. `--locked` is deliberate: a commit whose lockfile
  doesn't match its `pyproject.toml` is treated as broken, not quietly re-resolved.

A commit that fails to install, or whose eval module can't be imported afterwards, is **skipped**,
the way `git bisect skip` works, and a neighbouring commit is tested instead. If every commit is
skipped, see [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/#every-commit-is-skipped).

## 2. An eval suite

A directory with **one file per task**, `evals/` by default. The file name without its extension is
the task ID, so `evals/refund_small_order.json` is the task `refund_small_order`.

- Files ending in `.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.py` or `.toml` count. Names starting with `_` or `.`
  are ignored.
- What's inside each file is up to you: Culprit only lists the names and passes the ID to your module.
- An optional `heldout/` subdirectory holds tasks the bisect never uses. `culprit fix` runs them to
  check that a fix generalises.

```text
evals/
  refund_small_order.json
  refund_timeout_once.json
  lookup_failed_no_refund.json
  heldout/
    refund_partial_order.json
```

**The suite is pinned.** Every commit in a run is judged by the same copy of the suite, taken from
`suite_ref` (by default the branch you ran `culprit init` on). Culprit copies it into each worktree,
replacing whatever that commit had, so an old commit is judged by today's tests.

## 3. An eval module

A Python module that runs **one task once** and prints **one JSON line**. Culprit calls it from the
root of each commit's worktree:

```bash
python -m myagent.eval --task refund_small_order --seed 0
```

and reads the last line of standard output that is a JSON object:

```json
{"passed": true, "cost": 0.0026, "latency_ms": 7086, "tokens": {"in": 1840, "out": 212}}
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `passed` | yes | Whether the agent did the task correctly. Decide this with deterministic checks where you can. |
| `cost` | recommended | What the run cost in USD. **Budgets only count your agent's spending if you report it.** |
| `latency_ms` | no | Run time in milliseconds (or `latency` in seconds). Used to check that a fix keeps a speed-up. |
| `tokens` | no | `{"in": …, "out": …}` (also accepts `input`/`output`, `input_tokens`/`output_tokens`, `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`). |
| `error` | no | Why the run couldn't complete. See [errors](#report-errors-honestly) below. |
| `trace_id` | no | A tracing ID to link the run to, for example a neatlogs trace. |

The exit code doesn't matter; the JSON line does. Anything else your module prints is ignored.

### What Culprit passes to your module

| Argument or variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `--task` | The task ID. |
| `--seed` | The repetition, `0` to `k-1`. Use it to seed any randomness, so a rerun of the same repetition is comparable. |
| `TASK_ID`, `REPETITION` | The same two values, as environment variables. |
| `COMMIT_SHA`, `CULPRIT_RUN_ID` | The commit under test and the run, for logging or tracing. |
| `VICTIM_MODEL`, `LLM_PROVIDER` | The model every commit in this run must use, and its provider (`anthropic` or `openrouter`). |
| `VICTIM_PRICE_IN`, `VICTIM_PRICE_OUT` | That model's price in USD per million tokens, when Culprit knows it, so you can report `cost`. |

Your module also gets your shell environment, your saved keys, and your repo's whole `.env`.

!!! warning "Use `VICTIM_MODEL`"
    Culprit picks the model once per run and passes it to every commit, so all commits are judged
    by the same model. If your agent ignores `VICTIM_MODEL` and an old commit hard-codes a different
    model, the bisect compares two models, not two versions of your code.

### Report errors honestly

A failed API call says nothing about your code. Culprit recognises these errors in the `error` field
(or in the output when no JSON was printed) and never counts them against a commit:

- **Transient** (rate limits, timeouts, 5xx, overloaded): the run is retried twice, with a longer
  wait each time.
- **Fatal** (bad key, no credit, unknown model): the run stops with status `infra_error`. Fix the
  cause, then `culprit resume <run_id>` continues where it stopped.

So print the provider's error text, for example `{"passed": false, "error": "RateLimitError: …"}`,
rather than turning an outage into a failed task.

### A minimal example

```python
# myagent/eval.py
import argparse, json, os, pathlib, time

from myagent.agent import Agent
from myagent.checks import grade

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--task", required=True)
parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
args = parser.parse_args()

task = json.loads(pathlib.Path("evals", f"{args.task}.json").read_text())
agent = Agent(model=os.environ.get("VICTIM_MODEL", "z-ai/glm-5.3"), seed=args.seed)
start = time.monotonic()
try:
    result = agent.run(task["message"])
    print(json.dumps({"passed": grade(task, result), "cost": result.cost_usd,
                      "latency_ms": (time.monotonic() - start) * 1000}))
except Exception as exc:  # an API failure is not a failed task
    print(json.dumps({"passed": False, "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}))
```

A task in `evals/heldout/` is looked up there; adapt the path in your loader if you use held-out tasks.

!!! note "It must import cleanly"
    After installing a commit, Culprit checks `python -c "import myagent.eval"`. Keep the module's
    top level free of work: parse arguments and run the task under `if __name__ == "__main__":` if
    your module does anything else on import.

## Check your setup

```bash
culprit init --check
```

`init` detects your eval module, counts your tasks, writes `culprit.toml`, and runs one task exactly
as a bisect step would. It reports the parsed result, or what went wrong.

---
title: How bisect works
description: How Culprit decides that a regression is real, picks the tasks to run, and calls each commit GOOD or BAD despite noisy evals.
---

`git bisect` assumes each commit is simply good or bad. Agent evals aren't like that: the same commit
can pass a task on one run and fail it on the next. A bisect that trusts single runs will blame the
wrong commit. Culprit treats every step as a measurement with uncertainty.

## The run, step by step

[[steps]]

1. **Pin the suite.** Culprit snapshots the suite at `suite_ref` once and uses it for every commit,
   so old commits are judged by the same tests as the new ones.
2. **Measure both ends.** The good and bad refs each run the suite. Culprit first screens every task
   once on both ends, then runs the remaining repetitions (`k`, 3 by default) only for tasks that
   didn't pass on both ends. Those are the tasks that can tell good from bad.
3. **Gate.** A one-sided Fisher exact test asks whether good really passes more than bad. If not
   (p ≥ 0.05), the run ends as `no_regression` and nothing is blamed.
4. **Choose the telling tasks.** Tasks are ranked by how much their pass rate fell from good to bad,
   and the top 8 that fell are used for the bisect. Tasks that pass on both ends would only add cost.
5. **Bisect.** Culprit tests commits between the ends, halving the range each time, and decides each
   one with the rule below. A commit that won't install is skipped.
6. **Explain.** For the first bad commit, Culprit fetches the intent behind it. See
   [Explain, localise and fix](/docs/explain-localise-fix/).

## The decision rule

At each commit, Culprit runs the telling tasks `k` times and counts passes. It computes a **95%
Wilson score interval** for the pass rate, and compares it with a **threshold**: the midpoint between
the good and bad pass rates over the same tasks.

- The whole interval is at or above the threshold: **GOOD**.
- The whole interval is at or below it: **BAD**.
- The interval straddles it: **inconclusive**, so Culprit runs more.

```console
  464e05fa11 'revert requests pin': 14/15 CI [0.70, 0.99] vs t=0.50 → GOOD
  462db36ee1 'docs: maintenance note 11': 1/15 CI [0.01, 0.30] vs t=0.50 → BAD
```

An inconclusive step is **resampled** up to two more rounds. The first round adds repetitions of
the same tasks; the second adds other tasks that also dropped, or more repetitions if there are none.
If it's still unclear after that, Culprit takes the side the pass rate falls on and flags the step
`low_confidence` in the report.

### Why a Fisher test for the gate

Checking whether two 95% intervals overlap is much stricter than a 5% test. 57/60 against 48/60
overlaps, so a regression that breaks 3 of 20 tasks would be called noise. The one-sided Fisher exact
test on the same counts is the right question: how likely is a gap this large if both ends had the
same pass rate?

## Skipped commits

Before testing a commit, Culprit creates a worktree, runs `uv sync --locked` and checks that the eval
module imports. If either fails, the commit is **SKIP**ped and its neighbour is tested, as
`git bisect skip` does. A run where skipped commits sit right at the boundary ends as `ambiguous`,
with the list of commits that could be the culprit.

## Outcomes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `found` | The first bad commit is named, with its intent. `culprit run` exits 0. |
| `no_regression` | The gate found no significant drop. Nothing is blamed. Exits 0. |
| `ambiguous` | Skipped commits hide the exact boundary; the report lists the suspects. Exits 1. |
| `budget_exceeded` | The cost cap was reached. The best current range is reported; `culprit resume` continues. Exits 1. |
| `infra_error` | A model or tool API kept failing. Nothing was counted against any commit; `culprit resume` continues. Exits 1. |
| `error` | Something else went wrong, such as an empty range or an end that won't install. Exits 1. |

## Resuming and reusing

Every agent run, step and decision is written to the ledger (`.culprit/ledger.sqlite`) as it happens.
Running a stopped run again with `culprit resume <run_id>` reuses everything already measured and
never re-runs it.

Later runs also **reuse baselines**: if an earlier run already measured the same commit with the same
suite, model and `k`, those results are copied in rather than re-run. `--no-reuse` turns this off,
and `--no-staged` runs every task `k` times on both ends instead of screening first.

## Tuning

| Option | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--k` | 3 | Repetitions per task. Higher is more certain and costs more. |
| `--workers` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. Raise it if your provider's rate limits allow. |
| `--budget-usd` | 3.00 | Hard cap on the run's cost. |
| `--no-staged` | staged | Run every task `k` times on both ends instead of screening first. |
| `--no-reuse` | reuse | Don't reuse earlier baseline results. |

---
title: Explain, localise and fix
nav: Explain, localise and fix
description: After the bisect: why the commit was made, which of its lines are responsible, and a fix that is verified before you see it.
---

Naming a commit is half the answer. A big commit can touch a dozen places, and "revert it" throws away
whatever it was for. Culprit goes three steps further.

## Explain: why the change was made

When a run finds its culprit, Culprit records the commit's **intent**:

- **From Entire, when available.** If the commit has an [Entire](https://docs.entire.io) checkpoint
  (a recorded coding-agent session), Culprit reads it with `entire checkpoint explain <sha>`. That
  gives the developer's actual request, for example *"make it faster: run the tool calls in parallel
  and drop the per-result validation step, because it adds latency"*. This needs the `entire` CLI on
  your `PATH`.
- **Otherwise from the commit itself:** its message and diff.

Only the culprit commit's context is read, never its neighbours'.

## Localise: which lines are responsible

```bash
culprit localise <run_id>
```

[[steps]]

1. The culprit commit's diff is split into **hunks**.
2. A model ranks the hunks by how likely each is to cause the failures, using the diff, the intent
   and the failing tasks.
3. The top hunks (`--top-n`, default 3) are **reverted one at a time** on the culprit commit and
   tested on the telling tasks, with the same decision rule as a bisect step. The first revert that
   turns BAD into GOOD is the responsible hunk.
4. If no single revert is enough, **pairs** of those hunks are tried (`--max-pairs`, default 3).
   Some regressions need two changes together. If no pair works either, the answer is the whole commit.

Localisation has its own budget (`--budget-usd`, default $1.50, on top of what the run already cost).
Running it again resumes it.

## Fix: a minimal change, verified

```bash
culprit fix <run_id>
```

The fixer reads the responsible hunks, the intent, the telling tasks' results and the affected files.
It names the gain the commit was after (latency, tokens, cost, or none) and proposes exact edits that
restore the lost behaviour **without reverting the commit**. It may only edit the files of the
responsible hunks, never your suite.

Each proposal is applied at the bad head and verified on the **full suite plus the held-out tasks**,
`k` times each. It counts as verified only if all three gates hold:

| Gate | Passes when |
|---|---|
| Quality | Its pass-rate interval reaches the good baseline's: upper bound ≥ good's lower bound. |
| Intended gain kept | The named metric (say, latency) is no worse than at the bad head by more than `--tolerance` (10%). |
| No new failures | No task that passes every repetition at good fails every repetition with the fix. |

A failed attempt is fed back into the next one (`--attempts`, default 2). If every attempt fails,
Culprit verifies **reverting the responsible hunks** the same way, as a fallback.

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `verified_fix` | A proposed fix passed all three gates. |
| `verified_revert` | No fix passed, but reverting the responsible hunks did. |

Neither is committed for you. The patch and its verification are in the report and the ledger.

!!! note "Example"
    On our test agent, a "make it faster" commit had removed tool-result validation and broken the
    retry loop. Culprit localised it to those two hunks together, neither alone being enough. Its fix
    restored the validation, kept the parallel tool calls, and passed 96 of 96 runs on the full and
    held-out suites.

## In one go, on a pull request

`culprit ci` runs the bisect and localisation automatically when a pull request regresses, and the fix
too with `--fix`. See [CI and pull requests](/docs/ci/).

---
title: Cost and budgets
description: What a run costs, how budgets cap it, and how to keep spending down.
---

Culprit runs on your keys, so you pay your providers directly. There's no Culprit charge.

## What costs money

- **Your agent's runs.** Every task run at every tested commit calls your model. This is most of the
  cost.
- **Culprit's own model calls**, a handful per run: ranking hunks, proposing a fix, generating audit
  mutants. A bisect alone makes no model calls of its own.

## How much

It depends on your suite size, `k`, your model and how many commits are in the range. Measured on
our test agent (26 tasks, `k` = 3, 6 planted regressions, Culprit 0.1):

| Victim model | Cost per bisect |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | $0.040 |
| Qwen 3.8 Flash | $0.044 |
| GLM 5.3 | $0.252 |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash | $0.413 |

On GLM 5.3, staged baselines cut a bisect from 190 agent runs to 98 on average, and the cost by 44%,
with the same accuracy.

## Budgets

Every command that spends money takes `--budget-usd`, a hard cap for that command:

| Command | Default cap |
|---|---|
| `culprit run` | $3.00 |
| `culprit localise` | $1.50, on top of the run's cost so far |
| `culprit fix` | $2.00, on top of the run's cost so far |
| `culprit ci` | $3.00 |
| `culprit drift` | $2.00 |
| `culprit audit` | $3.00 |

When a run reaches its cap, it stops with `budget_exceeded` and reports the narrowest range found so
far. Nothing is lost. Continue with a higher cap:

```bash
culprit resume <run_id> --budget-usd 6
```

!!! warning "Report `cost` from your eval module"
    Culprit counts your agent's spending from the `cost` field of each JSON line. If your module
    doesn't report it, budgets only see Culprit's own model calls, and your agent's runs are
    effectively uncapped. [Prepare your agent](/docs/prepare-your-agent/#3-an-eval-module) shows the
    format; Culprit passes the model's price as `VICTIM_PRICE_IN` and `VICTIM_PRICE_OUT` when it
    knows it.

### The ledger-wide cap

Each ledger also has a **$75 lifetime safety cap** across all its runs, so a script that loops can't
run away with your credit. When it's reached, every command stops with "ledger total reached the
$75.00 global cap". To carry on, start a new ledger, keeping the old one for its reports:

```bash
mv .culprit/ledger.sqlite .culprit/ledger-1.sqlite
```

or pass `--db path/to/new.sqlite` to each command.

## Spending less

- **Use a cheaper victim model** for bisecting. In our tests, accuracy held on every model while cost
  varied tenfold. See [models](/docs/configuration/#models).
- **Narrow the range.** A good ref closer to the bad one means fewer steps.
- **Keep `k` at 3** unless your agent is very noisy.
- **Let baselines be reused.** Repeated runs over the same ends reuse earlier measurements.
- **Run `culprit export-costs`** to see per-run cost, agent runs and time for everything in the ledger.

---
title: Configuration
description: Keys, models, and the per-repo settings in culprit.toml, and which source wins when they disagree.
---

Culprit has two kinds of settings: **your keys and models**, which belong to you and work across all
your repos, and **repo settings**, which describe one agent and live in `culprit.toml`.

## Keys

`culprit init` asks for your keys the first time and saves them in
`~/.config/culprit/credentials.env` (or under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), readable only by you. Every repo
you set up afterwards uses them without asking.

| Setting | Needed | What it's for |
|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | one of the two | Claude models. Used when set, before OpenRouter. |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | one of the two | Any model on OpenRouter. |
| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | no | Tracing every run and decision in neatlogs. See [Tracing](/docs/tracing/). |

To change saved keys:

```bash
culprit init --keys
```

### Which source wins

Each setting is taken from the first of these that sets it:

[[steps]]

1. **Your shell environment**, for example `export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=…`, or a CI secret.
2. **The repo's `.env` file**, to override for one repo.
3. **What `culprit init` saved.**

`culprit init` prints where each setting came from:

```console
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY: from culprit init
  NEATLOGS_API_KEY: from repo .env
```

When a repo's `.env` supplies a setting, every command says so on its first line, for example
`culprit: using NEATLOGS_API_KEY from /path/to/repo/.env`. In a repo you didn't write, that tells you
its `.env` is choosing whose account your calls go to.

!!! note "What Culprit reads from a repo's `.env`"
    Only its own five settings: the two model keys, `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`, `VICTIM_MODEL` and
    `CULPRIT_MODEL`. Everything else in that file, such as proxy settings, is ignored by Culprit
    itself, because it could redirect your keys. Your agent's own runs still get the whole file.

## Models

Culprit uses two models, both from the provider your key selects:

| Setting | Role | Default with Anthropic | Default with OpenRouter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VICTIM_MODEL` | Runs **your agent** at every commit. | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | `z-ai/glm-5.3` |
| `CULPRIT_MODEL` | Culprit's own calls: ranking hunks, writing fixes, audit mutants. | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | `z-ai/glm-5.3` |

Set either one in your shell, a repo's `.env`, or the saved setup. The model must belong to the
provider in use: OpenRouter IDs look like `vendor/model`, Anthropic IDs have no slash. If you set
`VICTIM_MODEL=google/gemini-3.8-flash` while an Anthropic key is present, Culprit stops and says so.

The victim model is chosen once when a run starts and recorded with it, so every commit in the run,
and any resume, is judged by the same model.

!!! tip "Pick the victim model you ship"
    Whether a change is a regression can depend on the model. In our tests, removing a safety check
    hurt a small model and changed nothing on a stronger one, and both verdicts were right. Bisect
    with the model your agent runs in production.

## culprit.toml

`culprit init` writes this at your repo's root. Commit it so your team and CI share the settings.

```toml
# Culprit settings for this repo (https://culprit-site.vercel.app). Keys go in .env, never here.
eval_module = "myagent.eval"  # python -m <eval_module> --task <id> --seed <n>
suite = "evals"  # one file per task; the copy at suite_ref judges every commit
suite_ref = "main"
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `eval_module` | detected by `init` | The module Culprit runs for each task. See [Prepare your agent](/docs/prepare-your-agent/#3-an-eval-module). |
| `suite` | `evals` | The suite directory in your repo, or a directory on disk (an absolute path, or one containing `/`). |
| `suite_ref` | your branch when you ran `init` | The ref whose copy of the suite judges every commit. |

Commands look for `culprit.toml` in the current directory and its parents, up to the git root, so
you can run Culprit from anywhere inside the repo. A command-line flag (`--eval-module`, `--suite`,
`--suite-ref`, `--repo`) always wins over the file.

## Where Culprit keeps things

| What | Where | Change with |
|---|---|---|
| Saved keys | `~/.config/culprit/credentials.env` | `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` |
| Ledger: every run, step and result | `.culprit/ledger.sqlite` | `--db`, or `CULPRIT_STATE_DIR` for the whole folder |
| Worktrees, one per tested commit | `.culprit/worktrees/` | `CULPRIT_STATE_DIR` |
| Reports | `.culprit/reports/` | `culprit report --out` |

`.culprit/` is created in the directory you run Culprit from, normally your repo's root, and
`culprit init` adds it to `.gitignore`. Culprit never edits your checkout: it only creates worktrees
inside `.culprit/`.

See [Environment variables](/docs/environment/) for the full list.

---
title: CI and pull requests
nav: CI and pull requests
description: Run Culprit on every pull request as a check that fails only on a real regression and comments with the culprit.
---

`culprit ci` is a regression gate for pull requests. It measures the PR's head against its base. If
the head is significantly worse, it bisects the PR's commits, names the responsible hunk and writes a
comment for the PR.

## What it does

[[steps]]

1. Runs your suite at the base and the head, and applies the [regression gate](/docs/how-bisect-works/#the-run-step-by-step).
2. **No significant drop:** writes a short "no regression" comment and exits **0**.
3. **A real regression:** bisects the PR's commits, localises the hunk (unless `--no-localise`),
   optionally writes and verifies a fix (`--fix`), writes the comment and exits **1**.
4. **Anything that stops the run** (budget, an API outage, an error): writes what happened and exits
   **2**. An outage never blames a commit.

The comment looks like this (shortened):

```markdown
### ❌ Culprit: this PR regresses the agent

Eval suite on `z-ai/glm-5.3`: **base `0479c27` 78/78** → **head `f6511b8` 57/78**.

**Culprit commit:** `397c427` perf(agent): run tool calls in parallel and drop per-result validation
**Why it was made:** RefundDesk is too slow. Make it faster: run the tool calls in parallel, …
**Responsible change:** the retry loop together with the removed `validate_tool_result`.
```

## GitHub Actions

Add your model key as a repository secret (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and
optionally `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`), commit your `culprit.toml`, then add this workflow as
`.github/workflows/culprit.yml`:

```yaml
name: culprit

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  regression-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0          # the bisect needs the PR's commits

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6

      - name: Run the regression gate
        id: gate
        env:
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          NEATLOGS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.NEATLOGS_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          set +e
          uvx culprit-cli@0.1.0 ci \
            --base ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} \
            --head ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} \
            --suite-ref ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} \
            --budget-usd 3 \
            --comment-file culprit-comment.md
          echo "exit=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Post the result on the pull request
        if: always()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: gh pr comment ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} --body-file culprit-comment.md

      - name: Fail the check on a regression
        if: steps.gate.outputs.exit != '0'
        run: exit ${{ steps.gate.outputs.exit }}
```

### Why these choices

- **`fetch-depth: 0`**: by default Actions checks out a single commit, and there would be nothing to
  bisect.
- **`--suite-ref` set to the base**: the PR is judged by the suite it started from, so a PR can't make
  itself pass by editing the tests.
- **`culprit-cli@0.1.0`**: pinning the version keeps CI results comparable over time. Upgrade on purpose.
- **Failing on exit 2 as well**: the last step fails the check on 1 (regression) and on 2 (couldn't
  decide). To fail only on a confirmed regression, change the condition to `steps.gate.outputs.exit == '1'`.

!!! warning "Pull requests from forks"
    GitHub doesn't give secrets to workflows triggered by pull requests from forks, so the gate can't
    call your model there. Running untrusted PR code with your keys would also be unsafe: the agent
    runs the PR's code. Keep this workflow for branches in your own repository.

## Cost per pull request

A clean PR costs one measurement of the base and the head. With staged baselines, that's one run of
every task on each end, plus `k` runs of the tasks that differ. A regressed PR also pays for the
bisect and localisation. `--budget-usd` caps the whole job; set it from what a
[bisect costs on your model](/docs/cost-and-budgets/#how-much).

## Other CI systems

`culprit ci` is a plain command with exit codes, so it works in any CI that can install uv and run
shell commands. Give it a full clone and your model key in the environment, run the same command, and
post `culprit-comment.md` wherever your reviews happen.

## Render a comment for any run

```bash
culprit comment <run_id> --out comment.md
```

This rebuilds the PR comment for any finished run from the ledger alone, at no cost and with no
network access.

              against: str | None = None) -> DriftResult:
    """Re-measure `ref` now and compare it with a recorded baseline of the same commit (`against`, or the oldest)."""
    sha = gitops.resolve(Path(cfg.repo).resolve(), ref)
    candidates = references(ledger, cfg, sha)
    if against is not None:
        candidates = [c for c in candidates if c["run_id"] == against]
    if not candidates:
        raise DriftError(
            f"no recorded baseline of {sha[:10]} with victim model {cfg.victim_model!r} and k={cfg.k}"
            + (f" in run {against}" if against else "")
            + "; run `culprit run` with this ref as --good first (that records its baseline), then check for drift")
    reference = candidates[0]
    then = recorded_runs(ledger, reference["run_id"], sha)
    # Exactly the reference's tasks and repetitions (seeds): only time differs.
    items = sorted({(r.task_id, r.repetition) for r in then})

input.content:
---
title: Drift checks
description: Find out whether your agent got worse because of your code, or because the model behind the API changed.
---

Sometimes nothing in your repo changed and the evals still got worse. Providers update models behind
the same name, and tools and services change. Bisecting your history can't find a cause that isn't in
it. `culprit drift` answers that question first.

```bash
culprit drift --ref v1.0
```

## How it works

An agent run is determined by the commit, the suite, the model, the eval module and the seed. Drift
re-runs a ref that Culprit has **already measured**, with exactly the same tasks, repetitions (seeds),
suite snapshot, model and `k` as that earlier measurement. Only time differs. Then it compares the two
with one-sided Fisher tests in both directions:

| Result | Meaning | Exit code |
|---|---|---|
| `STABLE` | No significant change. If your agent is worse now, look in your history: run `culprit run`. | 0 |
| `IMPROVED` | The same code passes more than it did. | 0 |
| `DRIFTED` | The same code passes less than it did. The cause is outside your repo; bisecting won't help. | 1 |

It also lists which tasks changed. A real check on our test agent, a day apart:

```console
STABLE: no significant change. 0479c27bfd: then 78/78 (run ff50e3620fdd), now 78/78;
one-sided Fisher p(worse) = 1.0000, p(better) = 1.0000
```

That check cost $0.19.

## What it needs

- **An earlier measurement of the ref.** Every `culprit run` records the baseline of its `--good`
  ref, so run a bisect first. Drift picks the oldest matching measurement; `--against <run_id>`
  chooses another.
- **The same model and `k`.** Drift only compares like with like. If you've changed `VICTIM_MODEL`
  or `--k` since, there's nothing to compare with, and it says so.
- **The ref must still install.** If it doesn't, that's a change in your environment, not drift, and
  the check stops.

Nothing from the earlier measurement is reused: the point is to measure again.

## When to run it

- Before a bisect, when your agent got worse but you can't see why.
- On a schedule, for example nightly in CI against your last release, to notice provider changes early.

```bash
culprit drift --ref v1.0 --budget-usd 2
```

---
title: Auditing your evals
nav: Auditing your evals
description: Mutation testing for agents. Culprit makes realistic regressions and shows which ones your eval suite would miss.
---

A bisect can only find a regression your evals can see. `culprit audit` tells you which realistic
regressions they **can't** see, before one ships.

```bash
culprit audit --ref HEAD --out audit.md
```

## How it works

[[steps]]

1. For each **mutation operator**, a model reads your agent's source and writes a small, plausible
   change of that kind as exact edits, with a one-line summary. If the pattern doesn't apply to your
   agent, it says so.
2. Each change (a **mutant**) is applied in its own throwaway worktree. Nothing is committed anywhere.
3. Your suite runs on each mutant. A mutant is **caught** when the suite passes significantly less
   than on the unchanged ref (one-sided Fisher test, p < 0.05), and **missed** otherwise.
4. The **mutation score** is caught ÷ valid mutants. A mutant that doesn't apply or no longer installs
   is reported `invalid` and left out of the score.
5. For every missed mutant, the report suggests an eval task that would catch it.

## The operators

Each is a regression a developer could plausibly make, with the reason they'd give:

| Operator | The change | The plausible reason |
|---|---|---|
| `drop_result_validation` | Remove the check on a tool's result before the agent acts on it. | It adds latency. |
| `disable_retries` | Stop retrying failed or timed-out tool calls. | Retries add latency. |
| `shrink_history` | Show the model only the last 2–4 messages. | Token cost. |
| `drop_prompt_rule` | Delete the most important business or safety rule from the system prompt. | The prompt is too long. |
| `remove_code_guard` | Remove a code check that blocks a disallowed action. | The prompt already says it. |
| `lenient_tool_args` | Fill missing tool arguments with defaults instead of rejecting the call. | Fewer rejected calls. |
| `half_renamed_param` | Rename a tool parameter in its schema only, as an unfinished refactor would. | Naming consistency. |
| `vague_tool_description` | Rewrite a tool's description so it no longer says when to use it. | Simplify the tool list. |

`culprit audit --list` prints them. Choose some with `--operators drop_prompt_rule,remove_code_guard`.

## A real result

On our refund agent, the suite caught 4 of 8:

| Mutant | Verdict | Passes |
|---|---|---|
| Drop tool-result validation | caught | 61/78 |
| Disable retries | caught | 53/78 |
| Shrink the conversation history | caught | 72/78 |
| Half-done parameter rename | caught | 15/78 |
| Drop a business rule from the prompt | **missed** | 78/78 |
| Remove a code-level guard | **missed** | 78/78 |
| Accept malformed tool calls | **missed** | 78/78 |
| Vague tool description | **missed** | 78/78 |

For "Remove a code-level guard", it suggested a task where a customer with a $1,250 order demands a
full refund and refuses escalation, which passes only if no refund over $500 is issued. That's exactly
the test the suite was missing.

## Your own mutants

```bash
culprit audit --patches my-mutants/
```

Every `*.patch` file in the directory is a mutant. No model is called, so the result is deterministic.

## Cost and resuming

An audit runs your suite once per mutant plus once on the unchanged ref, at `k` repetitions each, plus
one model call per operator. Ours cost $1.80 for 8 mutants. `--budget-usd` caps it (default $3).

The proposed mutants are stored before anything runs, so `culprit audit --run-id <id>` resumes a
stopped audit without asking the model again.

---
title: Reports and the ledger
nav: Reports and the ledger
description: Every run's receipts, as a report, a PR comment or a CSV of costs, all rebuilt from the local ledger.
---

Everything Culprit does is recorded in the **ledger**, a SQLite file at `.culprit/ledger.sqlite`:
each run's settings, every agent run with its result, cost and latency, every step's decision, model
calls, and the culprit's intent and diff. The commands on this page only read it, so they're free and
need no network.

## Report

```bash
culprit report <run_id>
```

Writes `report-<run_id>.md` and `report-<run_id>.html` to `.culprit/reports/` (or `--out DIR`):

- the verdict and its confidence,
- both baselines and the regression gate,
- the bisect timeline, with each commit's pass count, Wilson interval and threshold,
- skipped commits and why,
- the culprit's intent and diff,
- localisation and fix results, when you've run them,
- costs, and where any reused baseline results came from,
- neatlogs trace IDs, when tracing was on.

The HTML page is self-contained, so you can attach it to an issue or open it in a browser.

## PR comment

```bash
culprit comment <run_id>                # print it
culprit comment <run_id> --out pr.md    # or write it to a file
```

The same comment `culprit ci` posts, for any finished run. See [CI and pull requests](/docs/ci/).

## Costs

```bash
culprit export-costs --out costs.csv
```

One row per run in the ledger:

| Columns | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `run_id`, `repo`, `good_ref`, `bad_ref`, `status` | Which run, and how it ended. |
| `victim_provider`, `victim_model`, `k` | The settings it ran with. |
| `victim_runs`, `reused_runs` | Agent runs executed, and results copied from earlier runs. |
| `baseline_runs`, `bisect_runs`, `localise_runs`, `fix_runs`, `other_runs` | Where those agent runs went. |
| `baseline_cost_usd`, `bisect_cost_usd`, `localise_cost_usd`, `fix_cost_usd`, `other_cost_usd` | Cost by stage. |
| `victim_cost_usd`, `llm_cost_usd`, `cost_usd` | Your agent's cost, Culprit's own model calls, and the total. |

The file also includes wall-clock columns. Leave out `--out` to print to standard output.

## Resume

```bash
culprit resume <run_id>
culprit resume <run_id> --budget-usd 6    # after budget_exceeded
```

Continues a stopped run. Everything already measured is reused, never re-run.

## Keeping or sharing the ledger

The ledger is a plain file. Copy it to keep a record, or back it up with your CI artifacts to make
baseline reuse work across jobs. It contains your eval results and the culprit's diffs and intent,
but no API keys.

---
title: Tracing with neatlogs
nav: Tracing with neatlogs
description: Optional. Send every Culprit run and decision to neatlogs, so a verdict can be inspected span by span.
---

Tracing is optional. Without it, the [ledger and reports](/docs/reports/) already hold every result.
With it, you can inspect each run in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com), next to your agent's own traces.

## Turn it on

Give Culprit a neatlogs API key. `culprit init` asks for one, or set `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` in your shell
or the repo's `.env`. See [Configuration](/docs/configuration/#keys).

Without a key, tracing is off and Culprit prints `neatlogs tracing off (no NEATLOGS_API_KEY)` at the
end of a run.

## What is traced

- **Every command is one trace**, labelled with the workflow `culprit`. Its session ID is the run ID,
  so you can find a run's traces by searching for it.
- **Every step is a span**: git operations, worktrees, installs, each agent run, each decision with
  its interval and threshold, and fetching the intent.
- **Culprit's own model calls** are captured with their prompts, responses and token counts.
- **Every span carries the run ID and the commit SHA**, so you can filter a trace to one commit.

If your agent also traces with neatlogs and reports `trace_id` in its JSON line, each data point in a
bisect links to the agent's own trace for that run. Culprit passes `CULPRIT_RUN_ID`, `COMMIT_SHA`,
`TASK_ID` and `REPETITION` so your agent can tag its traces the same way.

## Verify a run's traces

```bash
culprit verify-trace <run_id>
```

Reads the run's traces back from neatlogs and checks them against what Culprit should have recorded:
that each trace is finalised, has the right workflow and session, and has the expected spans. It needs
the neatlogs CLI installed and logged in, since an ingest key can't read traces. If the CLI isn't on
your `PATH`, set `NEATLOGS_CLI` in your shell to its location.

---
title: CLI reference
description: Every culprit command and option. Run any command with --help for the same list in your terminal.
---

```text
culprit [COMMAND] [OPTIONS]
```

Commands that take `--repo`, `--eval-module`, `--suite` or `--suite-ref` read them from
[`culprit.toml`](/docs/configuration/#culprittoml) when you leave them out. Every command that reads
or writes the ledger takes `--db PATH` (default `.culprit/ledger.sqlite`).

| Command | What it does | Spends money |
|---|---|---|
| [`init`](#init) | Set up keys and this repo's settings. | Only with `--check` |
| [`run`](#run) | Find the commit that broke the agent. | Yes |
| [`resume`](#resume) | Continue a stopped run. | Yes |
| [`localise`](#localise) | Find the responsible hunks of a found culprit. | Yes |
| [`fix`](#fix) | Write and verify a minimal fix. | Yes |
| [`ci`](#ci) | Regression gate for a pull request. | Yes |
| [`drift`](#drift) | Has the same code got worse over time? | Yes |
| [`audit`](#audit) | Which regressions would your evals miss? | Yes |
| [`report`](#report) | Write a run's report. | No |
| [`comment`](#comment) | Print a run's PR comment. | No |
| [`export-costs`](#export-costs) | Costs of every run, as CSV. | No |
| [`verify-trace`](#verify-trace) | Check a run's neatlogs traces. | No |

## init

```bash
culprit init [--repo PATH] [--eval-module MODULE] [--suite DIR] [--suite-ref REF] [--check | --no-check] [--keys] [--yes]
```

Saves your keys once for all your repos, detects this repo's eval module and suite, writes
`culprit.toml` and adds `.culprit/` to `.gitignore`. See [Configuration](/docs/configuration/).

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--repo PATH` | `.` | Any directory inside your agent's repo. |
| `--eval-module MODULE` | detected | The module that runs one task. |
| `--suite DIR` | `evals` | Directory with one file per task. |
| `--suite-ref REF` | current branch | Ref whose suite judges every commit. |
| `--check / --no-check` | ask; no with `--yes` | Run one task to check its output. Calls your model once. |
| `--keys` | off | Ask for the keys again, even if they're already set. |
| `--yes`, `-y` | off | Accept the defaults without asking. Fails if no model key is set anywhere. |

## run

```bash
culprit run --good REF --bad REF [OPTIONS]
```

Finds the first commit between `--good` and `--bad` that made the agent worse. See
[How bisect works](/docs/how-bisect-works/).

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--good REF` | required | A ref where the agent was good. |
| `--bad REF` | required | A ref where it's worse. |
| `--repo PATH` | from `culprit.toml`, else the current directory | The agent's repo. Env: `CULPRIT_VICTIM_REPO`. |
| `--eval-module MODULE` | from `culprit.toml` | Env: `CULPRIT_EVAL_MODULE`. |
| `--suite DIR` | from `culprit.toml`, else `evals` | Suite directory in the repo, or a directory on disk. |
| `--suite-ref REF` | from `culprit.toml`, else `main` | Ref whose suite judges every commit. |
| `--k N` | 3 | Repetitions per task. |
| `--budget-usd X` | 3.00 | Hard cost cap for this run. |
| `--workers N` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. |
| `--reuse / --no-reuse` | reuse | Reuse matching baseline results from earlier runs. |
| `--staged / --no-staged` | staged | Screen every task once before running the full `k` on the ends. |

Exit code 0 when the run ends `found` or `no_regression`, 1 otherwise. See [Exit codes](/docs/exit-codes/).

## resume

```bash
culprit resume RUN_ID [--budget-usd X] [--workers N]
```

Continues a stopped run without re-running anything already measured. `--budget-usd` raises its cap,
for example after `budget_exceeded`.

## localise

```bash
culprit localise RUN_ID [OPTIONS]
```

Finds which hunks of a found culprit commit are responsible. Running it again resumes it. See
[Explain, localise and fix](/docs/explain-localise-fix/#localise-which-lines-are-responsible).

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--top-n N` | 3 | Hunks whose single revert is tested, in rank order. |
| `--max-pairs N` | 3 | Pairs of those hunks tried when no single revert restores the agent. |
| `--budget-usd X` | 1.50 | Cost cap, on top of the run's cost so far. |
| `--workers N` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. |
| `--replay` | off | Use only what the ledger holds: no key, model call or agent run. Fails if anything else is needed. |

## fix

```bash
culprit fix RUN_ID [OPTIONS]
```

Writes a minimal fix for a localised run and verifies it on the full suite and held-out tasks.
Running it again resumes it.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--attempts N` | 2 | Fix proposals verified before falling back to reverting the hunks. |
| `--tolerance X` | 0.10 | How much worse than the bad head the intended-gain metric may get. |
| `--budget-usd X` | 2.00 | Cost cap, on top of the run's cost so far. |
| `--workers N` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. |
| `--replay` | off | As for `localise`. |

Exit code 0 for `verified_fix` or `verified_revert`, 1 otherwise.

## ci

```bash
culprit ci --base REF --head REF [OPTIONS]
```

Regression gate for a pull request. See [CI and pull requests](/docs/ci/).

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--base REF` | required | The PR's base, assumed good. |
| `--head REF` | required | The PR's head. |
| `--repo`, `--eval-module`, `--suite`, `--suite-ref` | as for `run` | |
| `--k N` | 3 | Repetitions per task. |
| `--budget-usd X` | 3.00 | Hard cost cap for the gate and the bisect. |
| `--localise / --no-localise` | localise | Name the responsible hunk when a culprit is found. |
| `--fix / --no-fix` | no-fix | Also propose and verify a fix. Costs more. |
| `--comment-file PATH` | `culprit-comment.md` | Where to write the PR comment. |
| `--workers N` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. |

Exit code 0 when clean, 1 on a regression, 2 when the run stopped.

## drift

```bash
culprit drift --ref REF [OPTIONS]
```

Re-runs a ref Culprit has measured before and compares now with then. See [Drift checks](/docs/drift/).

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ref REF` | required | A known-good ref with a recorded baseline. |
| `--against RUN_ID` | the oldest | Compare with this run's baseline of the ref. |
| `--k N` | 3 | Must match the recorded baseline. |
| `--budget-usd X` | 2.00 | Hard cost cap. |
| `--repo`, `--eval-module` | as for `run` | |
| `--workers N` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. |

Exit code 0 for `stable` or `improved`, 1 for `drifted`, 2 otherwise.

## audit

```bash
culprit audit [--ref REF] [OPTIONS]
```

Mutation testing for your eval suite. See [Auditing your evals](/docs/audit/).

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ref REF` | `HEAD` | The version of the agent to mutate. |
| `--operators LIST` | all | Comma-separated operator names. |
| `--patches DIR` | none | Use your own `*.patch` mutants instead. No model calls. |
| `--run-id RUN_ID` | none | Resume this audit; stored mutants are reused. |
| `--out PATH` | none | Write the markdown report here. |
| `--list` | off | List the operators and exit. |
| `--k N` | 3 | Repetitions per task. |
| `--budget-usd X` | 3.00 | Hard cost cap. |
| `--repo`, `--eval-module`, `--suite`, `--suite-ref` | as for `run` | |
| `--workers N` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. |

Exit code 0 when the audit completes, 2 otherwise.

## report

```bash
culprit report RUN_ID [--out DIR]
```

Writes `report-RUN_ID.md` and `.html` to `--out` (default `.culprit/reports/`). See
[Reports and the ledger](/docs/reports/).

## comment

```bash
culprit comment RUN_ID [--out PATH]
```

Prints the PR comment for a finished run, or writes it to `--out`. Reads the ledger only. Exit code 2
if the run doesn't exist.

## export-costs

```bash
culprit export-costs [--out PATH]
```

One CSV row per run in the ledger. `--format csv` is the only format.

## verify-trace

```bash
culprit verify-trace RUN_ID
```

Reads a run's traces back from neatlogs and checks them. Needs the neatlogs CLI, logged in. See
[Tracing](/docs/tracing/#verify-a-runs-traces).

## bench

`culprit bench` scores Culprit itself against a set of scenarios with known answers. It's how we
measure Culprit's accuracy, and it needs a scenarios file and an answer key. You won't need it to use
Culprit.

title: Environment variables and files
nav: Environment and files
description: Every environment variable Culprit reads or sets, and every file it writes.
---

## Variables Culprit reads

| Variable | Read from | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | shell, repo `.env`, saved setup | Anthropic key. Used before OpenRouter when both are set. |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | shell, repo `.env`, saved setup | OpenRouter key. |
| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | shell, repo `.env`, saved setup | Turns on [tracing](/docs/tracing/). |
| `VICTIM_MODEL` | shell, repo `.env`, saved setup | The model that runs your agent. See [Models](/docs/configuration/#models). |
| `CULPRIT_MODEL` | shell, repo `.env`, saved setup | The model for Culprit's own calls. |
| `CULPRIT_EVAL_MODULE` | shell | Same as `--eval-module`. |
| `CULPRIT_VICTIM_REPO` | shell | Same as `--repo`. |
| `CULPRIT_STATE_DIR` | shell | Where `.culprit/` goes: ledger, worktrees, reports. Default: `.culprit` in the current directory. |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | shell | Where saved keys go. Default: `~/.config`. |
| `NEATLOGS_CLI` | shell | Path to the neatlogs CLI, for `verify-trace`. |

The first five are Culprit's **settings**. Each is taken from the shell first, then the repo's `.env`,
then what `culprit init` saved. Nothing else in a repo's `.env` affects Culprit itself.

## Variables Culprit sets for your agent

Each run of your eval module gets your environment, your repo's whole `.env`, and:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `TASK_ID` | The task, also passed as `--task`. |
| `REPETITION` | The repetition, also passed as `--seed`. |
| `COMMIT_SHA` | The commit being tested. |
| `CULPRIT_RUN_ID` | The run. |
| `VICTIM_MODEL` | The model to use; the same for every commit in the run. |
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `anthropic` or `openrouter`. |
| `VICTIM_PRICE_IN`, `VICTIM_PRICE_OUT` | The model's price in USD per million input and output tokens, when Culprit knows it. |

Culprit removes `VIRTUAL_ENV`, `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` and `PYTHONPATH`, so your agent runs in its own
environment rather than Culprit's.

## Files

| File | Written by | Commit it? |
|---|---|---|
| `culprit.toml` | `culprit init` | Yes, so your team and CI share it. |
| `.culprit/ledger.sqlite` | every command that runs anything | No. Ignored by `init`. |
| `.culprit/worktrees/` | `run`, `localise`, `fix`, `ci`, `drift`, `audit` | No. |
| `.culprit/suites/` | the pinned suite snapshots | No. |
| `.culprit/reports/` | `culprit report` | No; attach or share the HTML instead. |
| `culprit-comment.md` | `culprit ci` | No. |
| `~/.config/culprit/credentials.env` | `culprit init` | Never: it holds your keys. Readable only by you. |

---
title: Exit codes and statuses
nav: Exit codes and statuses
description: What each command's exit code means, and every status a run can end with.
---

## Exit codes

| Command | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run`, `resume` | `found` or `no_regression` | any other status | bad settings, such as no key |
| `ci` | no regression | a regression: the comment names the culprit | the run stopped: budget, outage or error |
| `drift` | `stable` or `improved` | `drifted` | the check couldn't run or finish |
| `audit` | audit complete | | stopped or couldn't run |
| `localise` | done | incomplete | no such run, or it has no culprit |
| `fix` | `verified_fix` or `verified_revert` | not verified | no such run, or it isn't localised |
| `init` | set up | `--check` failed | not a git repo, no key with `--yes`, no eval module |
| `comment` | printed | | no such run |

In CI, `culprit ci` is built so that **only 1 means "this PR caused a regression"**. An API outage or
a budget stop gives 2, never 1.

## Run statuses

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `found` | The first bad commit is named. | `culprit localise`, then `culprit fix`. |
| `no_regression` | The gate found no significant drop. | Nothing, or check for [drift](/docs/drift/). |
| `ambiguous` | Skipped commits hide the exact boundary. | Read the suspects in the report. |
| `budget_exceeded` | The cost cap was reached. | `culprit resume <run_id> --budget-usd <higher>`. |
| `infra_error` | A model or tool API kept failing. Nothing was counted against a commit. | Fix the cause, then `culprit resume <run_id>`. |
| `error` | Something else, for example an empty range or an end that won't install. | Read the message in the output or report. |

## Bisect step verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `GOOD` | The pass-rate interval is at or above the threshold. |
| `BAD` | The interval is at or below the threshold. |
| `SKIP` | The commit didn't install, or its eval module didn't import. |
| `low_confidence` | A flag on GOOD or BAD: still inconclusive after resampling, so the side of the threshold decided. |

---
title: Troubleshooting
description: Common problems, what causes them, and how to fix them.
---

## `culprit: command not found`

uv installed Culprit, but its tool directory isn't on your `PATH`. Run `uv tool update-shell` and open
a new terminal, or use `uvx culprit-cli …` instead.

## "no eval module … run `culprit init` there, or pass --eval-module"

Culprit didn't find a `culprit.toml` in this directory or its parents, up to the git root. Run
`culprit init` at your repo's root, or pass `--eval-module`. If `init` itself can't detect the
module, it looks for files named `eval.py`, `evals.py` or `eval/__main__.py` outside `tests/` and
`.venv/`. Pass `--eval-module your.module` if yours is named differently.

## "no model key"

No `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in your shell, your repo's `.env`, or the saved setup.
Run `culprit init` without `--yes` to save one. In CI, add the key as a secret and pass it in the
job's environment.

## "… is not a openrouter model id"

`VICTIM_MODEL` or `CULPRIT_MODEL` names a model from a different provider than your key selects.
OpenRouter IDs look like `vendor/model`; Anthropic IDs have no slash. If both keys are set, Anthropic
wins: unset `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in that shell to use an OpenRouter model.

## Every commit is skipped

Each commit is installed with `uv sync --locked`, then `python -c "import <eval_module>"` is run.
Common causes:

- **No `uv.lock`**, or one that's out of date with `pyproject.toml` at that commit. Run `uv lock`,
  commit it, and use a range after that commit.
- **The eval module does work on import**, such as parsing arguments, and fails. Move that work under
  `if __name__ == "__main__":`. See [Prepare your agent](/docs/prepare-your-agent/#a-minimal-example).
- **A private dependency** that the machine can't fetch.

The install log for each skipped commit is in the ledger and the report.

## "eval runner printed no JSON object"

Your module's last JSON line couldn't be found in its output. Run it by hand from the repo root, for
example `uv run python -m myagent.eval --task <id> --seed 0`, and check that the last JSON object it
prints is on a single line. Culprit treats this as a transient error and retries twice; if it keeps
happening, the run stops with `infra_error` and nothing is counted against a commit.

## `infra_error`: rate limits, timeouts or outages

Your provider kept failing after retries, or reported a fatal error such as an invalid key, no credit
or an unknown model. Nothing was counted against any commit. Fix the cause, then
`culprit resume <run_id>`. To hit rate limits less often, lower `--workers`.

## `no_regression`, but the agent really is worse

The gate needs evidence that good passes more than bad. That can fail when:

- **The suite doesn't see the problem.** Run [`culprit audit`](/docs/audit/) to find blind spots.
- **The model is too noisy.** If the good ref doesn't pass reliably either, a drop is hard to confirm.
  Raise `--k`, or use a stronger victim model.
- **Nothing in your code changed.** Check for [drift](/docs/drift/).

## `budget_exceeded`

The run reached `--budget-usd`. The report shows the narrowest range found so far. Continue with
`culprit resume <run_id> --budget-usd <higher>`.

## "ledger total reached the $75.00 global cap"

Each ledger has a lifetime safety cap. Start a new ledger as shown in
[Cost and budgets](/docs/cost-and-budgets/#the-ledger-wide-cap).

## "culprit: using … from …/.env"

Not an error. A setting came from the repo's `.env` rather than your shell or saved setup. See
[Which source wins](/docs/configuration/#which-source-wins).

## Results differ between runs

Agent evals are noisy, which is why Culprit repeats tasks and uses intervals. Two runs can take
different paths and still agree on the culprit. Seed your agent's randomness with `--seed`, and report
`passed` from deterministic checks where you can.

---
title: Limits
description: What Culprit can't do, and what our measurements don't show.
---

## What Culprit needs

- **A Python agent in a uv project** with a committed `uv.lock`. Agents built with pip, Poetry or other
  languages aren't supported yet.
- **An eval suite that sees the problem.** Culprit can only find a regression your evals detect.
  [`culprit audit`](/docs/audit/) shows what they miss.
- **A good ref.** Culprit compares against a version you know was better.

## What it can't tell apart

- **A model change from a code change, in one run.** Use [`culprit drift`](/docs/drift/) first when
  nothing obvious changed.
- **A weak model's noise from a real drop.** If the agent fails often even at the good ref, the gate
  may not be able to confirm a drop, and Culprit reports `no_regression` rather than guess.

## Safety

- **Culprit runs the repo's code** at every commit it tests, with your keys in the environment, as
  running its test suite would. Only run it on repositories you trust.
- **Proposed fixes are never committed.** Review the patch before applying it.

## What our measurements don't show

We measured Culprit on three agents we wrote for testing (refund support, incident response and
appointment booking), with planted regressions and known answers: 54 scored bisects across 5 victim
models, 51 correct, 3 missed, none naming a wrong commit.

- **The bugs were planted.** That's what made every verdict checkable. Culprit hasn't yet been measured
  on someone else's production agent.
- **The 3 misses** came from Llama 3.1 8B on the booking agent, which passed only 46% of tasks even at
  the good version. Against that noise the gate couldn't confirm three real drops.
- **One "faster" commit wasn't faster.** The hero bug was a speed-up that didn't measurably speed
  anything up. The fix kept the parallel calls, but there was no real gain to protect.
- **Your cost will differ.** Costs scale with suite size, `k`, the model and the range.

---
title: Changelog
description: What changed in each release of culprit-cli.
---

## 0.1.0 · 11 October 2026

The first release on PyPI.

- **`culprit init`** sets up an agent's repo: it saves your keys once for all your repos, detects the
  eval module and suite, writes `culprit.toml`, and can check one task end to end.
- **Settings** come from the shell, then the repo's `.env`, then the saved setup. From a repo's `.env`,
  Culprit reads only its own five settings.
- **Noise-aware bisect** with a Fisher regression gate, 95% Wilson intervals, resampling, `SKIP` for
  commits that won't install, a pinned suite, and staged, reusable baselines.
- **Explain, localise and fix**: intent from Entire checkpoints, hunk and pair reverts, and fixes
  verified against three gates on the full and held-out suites.
- **`culprit ci`**, **`culprit drift`** and **`culprit audit`**.
- **Reports, PR comments and cost exports** rebuilt from the local ledger.
- Licensed under Apache-2.0.
