content.text:
The documentation is live at **https://culprit-site.vercel.app/docs/**, and the home page links to it.

**What's there:** 19 pages, laid out like the docs sites of tools such as promptfoo or Stripe.

| Section | Pages |
|---|---|
| Getting started | Introduction, Quickstart, Installation, Prepare your agent |
| Concepts | How bisect works, Explain/localise/fix, Cost and budgets |
| Guides | Configuration, CI and pull requests (GitHub Actions workflow), Drift checks, Auditing your evals, Reports and the ledger, Tracing with neatlogs |
| Reference | CLI reference (every command and option), Environment variables and files, Exit codes and statuses |
| Help | Troubleshooting, Limits, Changelog |

- **Navigation:** a sidebar, an "On this page" list that tracks your scroll, and prev/next links.
- **Search:** press `/` or ⌘K.
- **Reading aids:** copy buttons on code (they copy only the commands), coloured callouts, and a phone-friendly menu.
- **Same look as the home page:** dark, hairline grid, amber accent.

**Accuracy:**
- Every option, default, exit code and environment variable was checked against the code.
- The example outputs come from real runs.
- Writing the docs caught several mistakes, now fixed:
  - My own example eval module would have failed Culprit's import check.
  - The drift example had the wrong commit SHA.
  - The report page claimed contents the report doesn't have.
  - The home page's PR-comment mock mixed two different runs. It now shows only real comment text, and says where the intent quote comes from.

**Home page:** the nav has a Docs link, and Get started now reads `uv tool install culprit-cli` → `culprit init` → `culprit run`.

**Checked:** in a browser on desktop and phone, with no console errors, and every internal link and anchor resolves. After deploying, all pages return 200.

**For later:**
- **The $75 cap.** Each repo's ledger has a $75 lifetime safety cap left over from the hackathon setup, and users can't change it with a flag. The docs explain the workaround (start a new ledger). I'd make it a `--global-budget-usd` option in 0.1.1. That release will also carry the updated PyPI page text, which now leads with `uv tool install` and links the docs; it's already on `main`.
- **Updating the docs:** edit `docs-src/*.md`, run `uv run build_docs.py`, commit, then `vercel --prod`. Vercel isn't connected to the GitHub repo, so pushing alone doesn't redeploy.
- **No GitHub links yet,** as you asked. Tell me when to add them.

- **Heavy material sits at the bottom and is collapsed:** Concepts, Reference and Help.
- **Code blocks look clearly different from text,** each with a visible Copy button.
- **Text is larger and higher-contrast.**

I've made five docs designs for you to compare. All of them show the same Quickstart page with the same new menu, so the only difference is the look.

**The new menu (all five):**
```
Get started        Overview · Quickstart · Install · Prepare your agent
Workflow, in order ① culprit init     – set up keys and repo
                   ② culprit run      – find the culprit commit
                   ③ culprit localise – find the responsible lines
                   ④ culprit fix      – write and verify a fix
                   ⑤ culprit report   – read the receipts
More commands      ci · drift · audit · resume
▸ Concepts    (collapsed)
▸ Reference   (collapsed)
▸ Help        (collapsed)
```

**Also in all five:** larger body text (17–18px), higher contrast, and every command in its own block with a visible Copy button. The button copies only the command, never the `$` prompt or the output, and each command's output appears separately underneath.

| | Design | Look | What sets it apart |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | [Terminal Steps](https://claude.ai/artifact/TYcY5ESUt4BtJSqkbtBSvS) | Dark, like the home page | The command sequence is a connected timeline in the sidebar. Commands sit in terminal windows with an amber Copy button. |
| B | [Paper](https://claude.ai/artifact/UPB2aNMvfgXcVKFAX1wzcg) | Light, high contrast | The command sequence is boxed in the sidebar. Black code slabs on a white page are the most distinct from the text. |
| C | [Tabs](https://claude.ai/artifact/5NVg8gCnXEtPSEKhpD8Dtu) | Dark | Tabs along the top (Guide, Commands, Concepts, Reference, Help), so the sidebar never holds everything at once. Code blocks have a blue edge. |
| D | [Split](https://claude.ai/artifact/K8vvyK9ZyT383Vkbm1eRQy) | Light, warm | Explanation on the left; each step's commands and output in a dark column on the right, like Stripe's API docs. Uses a typeface designed for legibility. On phones it stacks into one column. |
| E | [Focus](https://claude.ai/artifact/SiV61wfcag3EW8zLixpb5b) | Warm dark | One centred column with the largest type. The sidebar is commands only, with no descriptions. The Copy button is built into the side of each command. |

input.content:
---
title: culprit init
description: Step 1. Save your keys once, and set up an agent's repo so every other command works without flags.
---

```bash
culprit init
```

Run it anywhere inside your agent's repo. It's safe to run again: it updates `culprit.toml` and only
asks for keys you haven't saved.

## What it does

[[steps]]

1. **Finds the repo root** and warns if there's no `uv.lock`, since Culprit installs each commit with
   `uv sync --locked`.
2. **Sets up your keys.** The first time, it asks which provider your model key is for, the key itself,
   and an optional neatlogs key. They're saved in `~/.config/culprit/credentials.env`, readable only by
   you, and used by every repo afterwards.
3. **Finds your eval module** (a file named `eval.py`, `evals.py` or `eval/__main__.py`) and counts the
   tasks in `evals/`.
4. **Writes `culprit.toml`** and adds `.culprit/` to `.gitignore`.
5. **Offers to run one task** exactly as a bisect step would, and shows the parsed result. This calls
   your model once.

```console
Setting up /home/you/refund-agent
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY: from culprit init
  your agent will run on z-ai/glm-5.3 via openrouter during a bisect
  eval modules found: refund_agent.eval
  26 tasks in evals/: refund_small_order, refund_timeout_once, …
  added .culprit/ to .gitignore
  wrote /home/you/refund-agent/culprit.toml
  check passed: task refund_small_order: passed=True (cost=0.0026, latency_ms=7086)
```

If it can't find an eval module, see [Prepare your agent](/docs/prepare-your-agent/).

## Common variations

Change your saved keys:

```bash
culprit init --keys
```

Skip the questions and the check, for scripts and CI:

```bash
culprit init --yes
```

Name the eval module and suite yourself:

```bash
culprit init --eval-module myagent.eval --suite evals --suite-ref main
```

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--repo PATH` | `.` | Any directory inside your agent's repo. |
| `--eval-module MODULE` | detected | The module that runs one task. |
| `--suite DIR` | `evals` | Directory with one file per task. |
| `--suite-ref REF` | current branch | Ref whose suite judges every commit. |
| `--check / --no-check` | ask; no with `--yes` | Run one task to check its output. |
| `--keys` | off | Ask for the keys again, even if they're already set. |
| `--yes`, `-y` | off | Accept the defaults. Fails if no model key is set anywhere. |

Exit code 0 when set up, 1 if `--check` failed, 2 if it couldn't set up (not a git repo, no key with
`--yes`, no eval module).

## Next

Commit `culprit.toml` so your team and CI share it, then [find the culprit](/docs/run/).

input.content:
---
title: culprit run
description: Step 2. Find the first commit between a good ref and a bad ref that made your agent worse.
---

```bash
culprit run --good v1.0 --bad HEAD --budget-usd 3
```

`--good` is any ref (tag, branch or commit) where the agent was good; `--bad` is one where it's worse.
Everything else comes from `culprit.toml`.

## What you'll see

```console
run 77f60c9fccf8: 14 commits in v1.0..HEAD, 10 tasks × 3
  screen ×1: good 9/10, bad 5/10; full k=3 on 5 tasks
  good 19/20 CI [0.76, 0.99]  bad 6/20 CI [0.15, 0.52]
  regression gate: one-sided Fisher p=0.0000 (alpha 0.05)
  discriminating tasks: t02, t04, t05, t01, t03
  4ebe03f827 install failed → SKIP
  464e05fa11 'revert requests pin': 14/15 CI [0.70, 0.99] vs t=0.50 → GOOD
  462db36ee1 'docs: maintenance note 11': 1/15 CI [0.01, 0.30] vs t=0.50 → BAD
  a6b1a67aaf 'docs: maintenance note 9': 14/15 CI [0.70, 0.99] vs t=0.50 → GOOD
  e38a2b4ed8 'speed up tool handling': 1/15 CI [0.01, 0.30] vs t=0.50 → BAD
Culprit: e38a2b4ed865a45a70d0ac149aa88204610620a8 'speed up tool handling' (confidence: 95% Wilson)
```

Reading it from the top:

- **The run ID** (`77f60c9fccf8`) is what `localise`, `fix`, `report` and `resume` take.
- **The ends** are measured first: good passed 19/20, bad 6/20.
- **The regression gate** checks the drop is real. Here p ≈ 0, so the bisect goes ahead.
- **Each bisect step** shows the commit, its passes, its 95% interval and the threshold, then GOOD,
  BAD or SKIP.
- **The last line** names the culprit.

[How bisect works](/docs/how-bisect-works/) explains each part.

## How it can end

| Status | Meaning | Next |
|---|---|---|
| `found` | The culprit is named. | [`culprit localise`](/docs/localise/) |
| `no_regression` | No significant drop. Nothing is blamed. | Check for [drift](/docs/drift/) |
| `ambiguous` | Skipped commits hide the exact boundary. | Read the suspects in the [report](/docs/report/) |
| `budget_exceeded` | The cost cap was reached. | [`culprit resume`](/docs/resume/) with a higher cap |
| `infra_error` | Your provider kept failing. Nothing was counted. | Fix the cause, then `culprit resume` |

Exit code 0 for `found` and `no_regression`, 1 otherwise.

## Common variations

More certainty on a noisy agent, at a higher cost:

```bash
culprit run --good v1.0 --bad HEAD --k 5 --budget-usd 6
```

Faster, if your provider's rate limits allow:

```bash
culprit run --good v1.0 --bad HEAD --workers 8
```

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--good REF` | required | A ref where the agent was good. |
| `--bad REF` | required | A ref where it's worse. |
| `--budget-usd X` | 3.00 | Hard cost cap for this run. |
| `--k N` | 3 | Repetitions per task. |
| `--workers N` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. |
| `--repo PATH` | from `culprit.toml` | The agent's repo. |
| `--eval-module MODULE` | from `culprit.toml` | The module that runs one task. |
| `--suite DIR` | from `culprit.toml`, else `evals` | The suite directory. |
| `--suite-ref REF` | from `culprit.toml`, else `main` | Ref whose suite judges every commit. |
| `--reuse / --no-reuse` | reuse | Reuse matching baseline results from earlier runs. |
| `--staged / --no-staged` | staged | Screen every task once before running the full `k` on the ends. |

## Next

[Find the responsible lines](/docs/localise/) with `culprit localise <run_id>`.

---
title: culprit localise
description: Step 3. Find which hunks of the culprit commit caused the regression.
---

```bash
culprit localise 77f60c9fccf8
```

Takes the run ID from [`culprit run`](/docs/run/). The run must have ended `found`.

## What it does

[[steps]]

1. Splits the culprit commit's diff into **hunks**.
2. Asks a model to **rank** them, using the diff, the commit's intent and the failing tasks.
3. **Reverts the top hunks one at a time** on the culprit commit and re-runs the telling tasks. The first
   revert that turns BAD into GOOD is the responsible hunk.
4. If no single revert is enough, **tries pairs** of those hunks. Some regressions need two changes
   together.
5. If no pair works either, the answer is the whole commit.

Each revert is judged with the same decision rule as a bisect step. See
[Explain, localise and fix](/docs/explain-localise-fix/).

## Cost and resuming

Localisation has its own cap, on top of what the run already cost: $1.50 by default. Running the same
command again resumes it, reusing every revert already measured.

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--top-n N` | 3 | Hunks whose single revert is tested, in rank order. |
| `--max-pairs N` | 3 | Pairs of those hunks tried when no single revert restores the agent. |
| `--budget-usd X` | 1.50 | Cost cap, on top of the run's cost so far. |
| `--workers N` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. |
| `--replay` | off | Use only what the ledger holds: no key, model call or agent run. |

Exit code 0 when done, 1 if incomplete, 2 if the run doesn't exist or has no culprit.

## Next

[Write and verify a fix](/docs/fix/) with `culprit fix <run_id>`.

---
title: culprit fix
description: Step 4. Write the smallest fix that restores the agent, keep what the commit was for, and prove it works.
---

```bash
culprit fix 77f60c9fccf8
```

Run it after [`culprit localise`](/docs/localise/) on the same run ID.

## What it does

[[steps]]

1. **Reads the evidence**: the responsible hunks, why the commit was made, the failing tasks and the
   affected files.
2. **Names what the commit was for**, such as lower latency or fewer tokens, so the fix can keep it.
3. **Proposes exact edits** that restore the lost behaviour without reverting the commit. It may only
   touch the responsible hunks' files, never your suite.
4. **Verifies the fix** at the bad head on the full suite plus your held-out tasks, `k` times each.
5. **Tries again** with the failure as feedback if a proposal doesn't pass (2 attempts by default),
   then falls back to verifying a revert of the responsible hunks.

A fix counts as verified only if it passes three gates:

| Gate | Passes when |
|---|---|
| Quality | Its pass-rate interval reaches the good baseline's. |
| Intended gain kept | The named metric is no worse than at the bad head by more than 10%. |
| No new failures | No task that always passed at good always fails with the fix. |

## The result

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `verified_fix` | A proposed fix passed all three gates. |
| `verified_revert` | No fix passed, but reverting the responsible hunks did. |

Nothing is committed for you. See the patch with [`culprit comment`](/docs/report/#pr-comment), review
it, and apply it yourself.

!!! tip "Add held-out tasks"
    Tasks in `evals/heldout/` are never used by the bisect, only to check that a fix generalises. A few
    of them make a verified fix much more trustworthy.

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--attempts N` | 2 | Fix proposals verified before falling back to reverting the hunks. |
| `--tolerance X` | 0.10 | How much worse than the bad head the intended-gain metric may get. |
| `--budget-usd X` | 2.00 | Cost cap, on top of the run's cost so far. |
| `--workers N` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. |
| `--replay` | off | Use only what the ledger holds. |

Exit code 0 for `verified_fix` or `verified_revert`, 1 otherwise.

## Next

[Read the report](/docs/report/) with `culprit report <run_id>`.

---
title: culprit resume
description: Continue a run that stopped, without re-running anything already measured.
---

```bash
culprit resume 77f60c9fccf8
```

Every agent run and decision is saved to the ledger as it happens. `resume` picks up where the run
stopped and reuses everything already measured.

## When you need it

| The run ended with | Do this |
|---|---|
| `budget_exceeded` | Resume with a higher cap: `culprit resume <run_id> --budget-usd 6` |
| `infra_error` | Fix the cause (key, credit, outage), then `culprit resume <run_id>` |
| You pressed Ctrl-C | `culprit resume <run_id>` |

```bash
culprit resume 77f60c9fccf8 --budget-usd 6
```

The run keeps its original settings, including the model, so every commit is still judged the same way.

`localise`, `fix` and `audit --run-id` resume the same way: run the same command again.

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--budget-usd X` | unchanged | Raise the run's cost cap. |
| `--workers N` | 4 | Agent runs in parallel. |
| `--db PATH` | `.culprit/ledger.sqlite` | The ledger holding the run. |

Exit code 0 when the run ends `found` or `no_regression`, 1 otherwise.

content.text:
The docs now use design A, with the original site's font sizes and layout. It's live at **https://culprit-site.vercel.app/docs/**.

**What changed:**
- **Sidebar order:**
  1. Get started: Overview, Quickstart, Install, Prepare your agent, Keys and configuration.
  2. Workflow, in order: a numbered amber timeline of `culprit init → run → localise → fix → report`, each with a one-line description. The current step's circle is filled.
  3. More commands: `ci`, `drift`, `audit`, `resume`.
  4. Concepts, Reference and Help: folded at the bottom. Each opens on its own when you're on one of its pages.
- **One page per command.** I added `init`, `run`, `localise`, `fix`, `report` and `resume`. Each has the command at the top, what it does, sample output, common variations, an options table, exit codes and a "Next" link to the following step. The full CLI reference is still under Reference.
- **Code blocks:**
  - Commands sit in a terminal window with a `$` prompt and an always-visible amber Copy button. It copies only the commands and turns green when copied.
  - Output sits in a dashed box underneath and can't be copied.
  - Python, YAML and other code gets a labelled window with its own Copy button.

---
title: Quickstart
description: Install Culprit and find your first culprit commit.
---

You need Python 3.12 or newer, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git, and an API key from
[Anthropic](https://console.anthropic.com/) or [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/). Culprit is
developed on macOS and meant for Linux CI runners too; Windows hasn't been tested.

## Install

```bash
uv tool install culprit-cli
```

This puts the `culprit` command on your `PATH`. If your shell can't find it afterwards, run
`uv tool update-shell` and open a new terminal.

Other ways: `pipx install culprit-cli` or `pip install culprit-cli`. To try a command without
installing, prefix it with `uvx culprit-cli`, as in `uvx culprit-cli init`. Culprit needs uv on your
`PATH` either way, because it installs your agent with it.

## Your first bisect

Your agent's repo needs an eval module and a suite first. [Prepare your agent](/docs/prepare-your-agent/)
covers what they look like.

[[steps]]

1. **Set up the repo.** Saves your key and writes `culprit.toml`.
    See [`culprit init`](/docs/init/).

    ```bash
    culprit init
    ```

2. **Find the commit.** Give it a ref that was good and one that is bad. It prints a run ID.
    See [`culprit run`](/docs/run/).

    ```bash
    culprit run --good v1.0 --bad HEAD --budget-usd 3
    ```

3. **Find the lines and fix them**, using that run ID. See [`culprit localise`](/docs/localise/) and
    [`culprit fix`](/docs/fix/).

    ```bash
    culprit localise 77f60c9fccf8
    culprit fix 77f60c9fccf8
    ```

4. **Read the report.** See [`culprit report`](/docs/report/).

    ```bash
    culprit report 77f60c9fccf8
    ```

## Upgrade or uninstall

```bash
uv tool upgrade culprit-cli
uv tool uninstall culprit-cli
```

Uninstalling leaves your saved keys and each repo's `.culprit/` folder and `culprit.toml` in place.
[Where Culprit keeps things](/docs/configuration/#where-culprit-keeps-things) lists them. The
[changelog](/docs/changelog/) says what each version changed.

## Next

[[cards]]

- [CI and pull requests](/docs/ci/): run the check on every pull request.
- [How bisect works](/docs/how-bisect-works/): why Culprit can trust noisy evals.

---
title: Overview
description: Culprit finds the commit that made your AI agent worse, using your own eval suite and real statistics, then explains it and verifies a fix.
---

Your agent passed its evals last week. Today it fails some of them, and dozens of commits sit in
between. Culprit is `git bisect` for that situation, built for noisy evals: it repeats every
measurement, decides with confidence intervals, and blames nothing when the drop could be noise.

It runs on your machine with your own model key, needs no SDK in your agent, and records every
decision so you can check it.

## The workflow

| Step | Command | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [`culprit init`](/docs/init/) | Your key saved, your repo set up. |
| 2 | [`culprit run`](/docs/run/) | The commit that made the agent worse, and why it was made. |
| 3 | [`culprit localise`](/docs/localise/) | The lines in that commit that did it. |
| 4 | [`culprit fix`](/docs/fix/) | A minimal fix, verified on your suite and held-out tasks. |
| 5 | [`culprit report`](/docs/report/) | The receipts: every step, interval and cost. |

Beyond one-off bisects: [`culprit ci`](/docs/ci/) gates every pull request,
[`culprit drift`](/docs/drift/) tells you whether the model behind the API changed, and
[`culprit audit`](/docs/audit/) shows which regressions your evals would miss.

## Results so far

On three test agents with planted regressions and known answers, Culprit ran 54 scored bisects across
5 victim models: **51 correct, 3 missed, none naming a wrong commit**. [Limits](/docs/limits/) explains
the misses and what these results don't show.

## Start here

[[cards]]

- [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart/): install and run your first bisect.
- [Prepare your agent](/docs/prepare-your-agent/): the eval module and suite Culprit expects.

content.text:
The home page is now short and visual, and all the detail is on a new **Case study** page. The first deploy didn't complete; the second did, and all pages return 200. Live at https://culprit-site.vercel.app.

**Home page** (about half its old length), top to bottom:
1. **Hero:** headline, one sentence, the install command with a Copy button, and the replayable 14-commit bisect, which is a real run.
2. **How it works:** three short steps, one command each: `run`, `localise`, `fix`.
3. **"One run can't tell good from bad":** an interactive interval demo. Pick a preset or drag the sliders, and the 95% interval tightens until it clears the threshold:
   - 1 run that passed gives "run more", because the interval is [0.21, 1.00].
   - 21 of 21 gives GOOD at [0.85, 1.00], the same numbers the real bisect logged.

   It uses the same formula Culprit does.
4. **Three product cards with small visuals:**
   - `ci`: a GitHub-style checks list with the culprit check failing.
   - `drift`: then/now bars and a STABLE pill.
   - `audit`: a grid of caught and missed mutants.
5. **One line of proof** ("0 wrong commits in 54 bisects, on 3 agents and 5 models") with a button to the case study.

**Case study** (`/case-study/`, in the top nav):
- The headline numbers.
- A table scoring all 54 bisects against the answer key.
- The "make it faster" bug start to finish, as a timeline: the drop, the bisect, the intent quote, the two hunks, and the 96/96 fix.
- Cost per model and the v1 → v2 savings.
- The model × bug grid and the two other agents.
- Links to the real drift and audit results.
- The caveats.

Nothing is repeated: the docs now link to the case study for results, costs, caveats and the worked example. I checked both pages in the browser, the interval demo works, and every link across the 21 pages resolves.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Replays the recorded hero story at $0, for screen recording:
#   culprit report → culprit localise --replay → culprit fix --replay
# Everything comes from a copy of the ledger. No model call, no victim run, no trace export, and no
# network: the keys are blanked, uv runs offline, and scripts/no_network blocks internet sockets in
# the culprit process. The real ledger is only read (an SQLite backup), never written.
#
#   scripts/demo_replay.sh [run_id]          # default: the hero run ff50e3620fdd
#   CULPRIT_DB=/path/ledger.sqlite DEMO_PAUSE=0 scripts/demo_replay.sh <run_id>
set -euo pipefail

RUN_ID="${1:-ff50e3620fdd}"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SOURCE_DB="${CULPRIT_DB:-$ROOT/.culprit/ledger.sqlite}"
PAUSE="${DEMO_PAUSE:-2}"
WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/culprit-replay.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

[ -f "$SOURCE_DB" ] || { echo "no ledger at $SOURCE_DB (set CULPRIT_DB)" >&2; exit 2; }

# Empty values, not unset: the CLI loads .env, which would otherwise put the keys back.

DB="$WORK/ledger.sqlite"

py() { uv run --project "$ROOT" --frozen --offline --quiet python "$@"; }
culprit() { uv run --project "$ROOT" --frozen --offline --quiet culprit "$@"; }
stage() { printf '\n\033[1m━━ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; sleep "$PAUSE"; }

import sqlite3, sys

PY
}

import sqlite3, sys
src = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{sys.argv[1]}?mode=ro", uri=True)  # consistent even while another process writes

src.backup(dst)
dst.close()
PY
